Revision Techniques That Work

Research suggests that testing yourself is more effective than re-reading notes. Flashcards and past papers are good ways to practise recall.

Spacing revision over several weeks works better than cramming the night before. Short sessions of about 30 minutes with breaks help concentration.

Sleep matters too: memories are strengthened during sleep, so staying up all night before an exam is counterproductive.

Finally, explaining a topic out loud to someone else can reveal gaps in understanding.
